name: Question 1
problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & 2 \\ 0 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are eigenvectors that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=1$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-4$ of the matrix $A,$ given above. Find the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}=[a,\,b,\,c]^{T}$ such that the set ${{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}}$ is linearly independent. What is the value of $\frac{a}{b}?$
worked_solution:
Since $A$ is an upper triangular matrix, we have that its eigenvalues are the entries in the main diagonal, that is, ${\lambda }_{1}=1,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=-4$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=5.$ 

Also, since we obtained three distinct eigenvalues, the set of eigenvectors ${{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}},$ where each vector corresponds to different eigenvalue, will be linearly independent.

Now, recall that ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=1$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-4.$ Thus, the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}$ must correspond to ${\lambda }_{3}=5.$ 

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =5.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & 2 \\ 0 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}]-5[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 7 & 2 \\ 0 & -9 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-4{x}_{1}+7{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=0 \\ -9{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the augmented matrix $M$ is already in its row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 7 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -9 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=\frac{2}{9}{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{1}{4}(7{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(7(\frac{2}{9}{x}_{3})+2{x}_{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{32}{9}{x}_{3} \\  & =\frac{8}{9}{x}_{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{8}{9}{x}_{3} \\ \frac{2}{9}{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{3}=9,$ we get the following eigenvector:

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 2 \\ 9\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{8}{2}=4.$
